newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch coffee firm buys units from Israel's Elite.
newsitem.headline: Dutch coffee firm buys units from Israel's Elite.

text.p: Privately owned Dutch coffee roaster Drie Mollen BV said on Monday it had acquired the French and Spanish coffee activities and some German coffee brands from Elite Industries of Israel.

"With this transaction Drie Mollen will increase its sales by 160 million guilders to approximately 460 million guilders, thus becoming the largest private label coffee roaster in Europe," the Dutch company said in a statement.
It gave no financial details of the deal but said the companies acquired, which employ a total of 120 people, will continue to operate under their own names.

Drie Mollen said it expected to increase profitability of the companies by exploiting synergies in production, by boosting the product ranges to including instant coffee and tea, and by efficiency measures.

After the acquisitions Drie Mollen will have 13 companies throughout the Netherlands, France, Germany, Lithuania, Poland, Russia, Spain and Britain, employing over 600 people. --Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
